items.heading: IICRC
items.text: Sets the technical standards for water damage restoration. Confirm a company's technicians hold real, current IICRC certification before you hire them.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 2.5s6 7 6 11.5a6 6 0 0 1-12 0c0-4.5 6-11.5 6-11.5z"/></svg>
items.heading: EPA
items.text: The federal government's own guidance on drying out a water-damaged home fast enough to keep mold from taking hold.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M7 3h7l4 4v14a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H7a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V4a1 1 0 0 1 1-1z"/><path d="M14 3v4h4"/><path d="M9 13h6M9 17h6M9 9h2"/></svg>
items.heading: RIA
items.text: A national trade association whose member companies agree to a written code of ethics covering honest estimates, safety, and fair billing.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="3" y="7" width="18" height="10" rx="1"/><path d="M3 12h18M8 7v10M16 7v10"/></svg>
items.heading: NADCA
items.text: Sets the industry standard for inspecting and cleaning HVAC systems after water damage, so contaminated ductwork doesn't spread moisture through the rest of the house.

items.heading: BBB
items.text: Look up any restoration company's complaint history, customer reviews, and accreditation status — a free, independent check before you hire.
